text:
mike: Heads up — since ~03:10 we've had a spike of GPU attach failures in ap-southeast1. Lots of pending jobs stuck waiting for nodes. I can see attach queue growing from 20->180 in 6m. Correlates with an NVMe IOPS spike on local scratch and repeated SMART temp cycles on a subset of hosts. Anyone digging in?

ops-bot: alert: ap-southeast1: nodepool-scratch: high iops (90th=14k r/s), attach-failures=142, janitor-deep-scrub started 2026-03-23T03:12:18Z

anya: i'm on it. looking at metrics — nodes with >75C spikes on nvme show scrub churn every ~60s (thermal cycling). Looks like scrub runner is doing full-pass retries when it hits transient read errors. That pushes qdepth and causes IO waits; GPU attach times out.

sara: grabbing a sample from one host: ```
2026-03-23T03:13:05 host-apse1-07 kernel: nvme nvme0: temperature threshold exceeded: 78C -> 72C
iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s     w/s   %util
nvme0n1        3200   45000   99.8
```

mike: oh nice — scrub overlapping with bulk warp snapshot job at 03:11. Janitor job triggered deep-scrub on ~120 hosts in the same window.

anya: confirmed. scrub controller has burst_concurrency=200 (default). We should throttle to 40 for ap-southeast1 due to known thermal headroom. Also set scrub_retry_backoff to exponential so we don't hammer devices on transient read retries.

kevin: i can push a hotfix to the janitor config and roll a canary in ap-southeast1. Proposed changes: burst_concurrency=40, io_throttle_pct=6, backoff_base=2s. Will also add metric for scrub_retry_count.

mike: good. temporary mitigation: mark two scratch nodepools as avoid_attach (nodepool labels) so new GPU jobs schedule to dedicated-ssd-pool until canary is green. Note: cross-region fallback isn't acceptable for latency-sensitive customers and adds egress cost.

sara: queued the label change for 03:28; canary config ready for kevin. Also raised a postmortem tag on the incident.

kevin: rolling canary now. I'll monitor attach success rate and gpu-attach latency. ETA for canary assessment 10m.

ops-bot: canary-deploy: janitor-config v2026.03.23-hotfix started on ap-southeast1 (10 hosts). monitor: attach-failures -> 12 (down from 142)

anya: early signal looks good — attach queue drained. follow-ups: root cause doc, add region-specific scrub profiles, and a long-term plan to cap concurrent scrubs when avg NVMe temp >70C.

mike: assign to kevin/anya for the follow-up. thanks all :thumbsup:
